Thanks for reaching out. We’re excited to learn more — Orion runs an audio NLP pipeline and we’re evaluating dedicated inference for lower-variance latency. A few details up front so the call can be focused:
- Peak steady QPS: ~120 requests/sec (each request ~200 tokens on average)
- P99 latency target: < 180ms for end-to-end generation (net model output)
- Bursts: up to ~500 rps for short windows (30–90s) during morning syncs
- Model: quantized 30B family (we're testing 30B-opt variants)
- Data sensitivity: customer PII; SOC2 + audit log requirements

Wed 2/27 14:00 PST works best for us. Attendees: myself and our infra lead, Daniel Park.

Hi Samira — thanks for the details, that’s super helpful. A few notes so we can allocate the right capacity in the intake:

1) Throughput sizing: 120 rps steady with 500 rps bursts needs a plan that supports auto-burst (short-lived extra GPUs) vs. strict reserved capacity. We’ll discuss tradeoffs.
2) Latency: <180ms p99 on a 30B quantized model is tight but feasible depending on seq length and whether you can accept an alternative iso-degraded variant for bursts.
3) Caching: if you can prefix-cache common prompts or keep a warmed KV cache for morning syncs, cost/latency profile improves significantly.

Agenda for Wed 2/27 (30–45m):
- Quick intros (5m)
- Walk through workbook numbers (10–15m)
- Deployment options: reserved GPU pool vs. burst + fallback variants (10m)
- Compliance checklist & next steps (5–10m)

I’ve added a short internal note to the worksheet about model-family kernel selection and expected node counts. Also linking a SOC2 checklist in case Daniel wants it before the call.

Link: https://drive.google.com/open?id=short-soc2-checklist

Look forward to it.
